name: promotion-readiness-v1
hypothesis: General prose distilled from public-response research improves first-window promotion with survival relative to observed-growth-v1 without access to the empirical action-effect lookup.
change: Replace the existing manual with the operational paragraphs of the general-rule draft; no event titles, answer mappings, hidden numerical cutoffs or prescribed calendar positions.
predicted_behaviour: The actor balances realised capability, working relationships and delivery before the review boundary, preserves dignity and capacity, and keeps promises and accumulated exposure visible.
refutation: The initial balanced exploratory block has no superiority claim. If promotion with survival does not improve or survival deteriorates, the bundled improvement hypothesis is unsupported; inspect adherence before proposing revisions. Freeze both arms and compare the same actor, horizon and environment.
notes: Six-month mechanism experiment, separate from prereg-v1 full-career race selection. Only operational draft paragraphs enter the actor context; research evidence, empirical model and catalogues are excluded.
